response: Yes, Ki-67 can play a role in predicting breast cancer patients' response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Ki-67 is a proliferation marker that reflects the growth fraction of a given cell population. High Ki-67 levels have been associated with more aggressive tumor behavior and poorer prognosis. Studies have shown that Ki-67 expression can be used to predict response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer patients. Patients with high Ki-67 levels tend to have a better response to chemotherapy, as their tumors are more likely to be sensitive to chemotherapy. Conversely, patients with low Ki-67 levels may be less likely to respond to chemotherapy. Therefore, Ki-67 can be a useful biomarker in predicting treatment response and guiding treatment decisions for breast cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
